title: Mother's Promise
selection_exposition: Many years before D Block calls him the Champ, young Rico lives with his mother, Anne, in the poor settlements beyond Nortune's outer wall.<New>As Anne's illness worsens, one cold day becomes a turning point in Rico's life.<New>Though Anne passes away when Rico is only ten years old, the words she leaves behind remain with him, shaping the man he will one day become...<Close>
blocks:
CHAPTER 1
MOTHER'S PROMISE<Close>

[Long before D Block called him
the Champ, Rico lived with his
mother in the poor settlements
beyond Nortune's outer wall.]<Close>
Rain streaks the glass. Beyond the low roofs, Nortune's outer wall rises beneath a pale sky.<Close>
The road toward Nortune's gate is gray with rain.<New>The poor settlement huddles outside the Imperial Capital's wall.<Close>

Anne
Rico... come closer, my sweet boy. Don't hide your hands from me.<Close>

<Rico>
The kids near the city gate called me a beast today, Mom. They threw stones. They said monsters like me don't belong in Kislev.<Close>

Anne
Listen to me carefully, Rico. People often fear what they do not understand.<New>Sometimes that fear hardens into hate.<Close>

<Rico>
It hurts, Mom.<Close>

Anne
What those children did was cruel. Their violence does not excuse violence in return.<New>If you hurt them back, the hatred only finds a new home. Mercy is choosing to end that cycle.<New>Your body is strong, but keep your heart gentle. Never let their cruelty decide who you become.<Close>

<Rico>
I'll try, Mom.<Close>

Anne
I know you will.<New>Now... help me with a few tasks today, alright?<Close>
[Anne turns away and raises the cloth to her mouth. When she lowers it, Rico sees blood.]<Close>

<Rico>
There is blood again. The medicine isn't helping.<New>Tell me what to do, Mom. I can find another doctor.<Close>

Anne
The doctors can do no more.<New>This sickness will take me soon.<Close>

<Rico>
No. There must be something I can do.<New>I can't just let you die.<Close>

Anne
You cannot fight this sickness for me, my sweet boy.<New>But you can choose what you carry after I am gone.<Close>

<Rico>
What do you want me to carry?<Close>

Anne
Mercy.<New>After I am gone, you may feel angry at the whole world.<New>Do not make others suffer because you are suffering.<New>One day, you may have power over those who looked down on you.<New>Use that power to protect people, not to take revenge.<New>Then the cruelty that wounded us will end with you.<New>Promise me.<Close>

<Rico>
I will. I promise.<Close>
[The camera holds on Rico, then eases back to the wide graveside tableau.]<Close>
END OF CHAPTER 1<Close>

Anne
Rico, would you fetch some water from the bucket and make me some tea?<Close>

<Rico>
The stove is on, Mom. It'll boil soon.<New>Anne
Thank you, Rico.<Close>

Anne
Second... take another scoop of water from that same bucket.<New>Give a drink to the stonebell in the vase on the table.<New>Then open the woodstove valve so more heat can spread through the house.<Close>

Anne
Do you remember where you found that stonebell, Rico?<New><Rico>
In the streets near the market.<New>I felt bad because it was stepped on.<New>Remember you said we could try to save it?<Close>

Anne
Yes, I remember.<New>That stonebell is the most precious gift I've ever received.<New>Look how healthy it is now because you've been taking care of it.<New>Stonebells take root between bare stones, where almost nothing else can grow.<New>Still, their pale blue bells always turn toward the light.<New>You have a good soul, Rico.<New>Never let this world forget that.<New><Rico>
I won't, Mom...<Close>

Anne
Rico, the fire in the woodstove won't last through tonight.<New>Would you bring in the dry slats stacked outside beside the house?<Close>

<Rico>
I'll be just outside. Call if you need me.<Close>

Anne
I will.<New>Take only what you can carry. The rest can wait.<Close>

Anne
The dry slats are stacked just outside, beside the house.<New>Take only what you can carry, Rico.<Close>

Outside their house, pale daylight lies over the settlement beyond Nortune's outer wall.<New>Beside the house, Rico pulls the driest slats from the broken packing crate and gathers a small armful for the stove.<New><Rico>
These will burn.<New>This should keep Mom warm tonight.<Close>
As night falls, Rico feeds the woodstove until the room is warm, but Anne's shivering has not stopped.<Close>

<Rico>
The fire is warm now.<New>Why are you still shaking?<Close>

Anne
This sickness has been with me a long time.<New>Tonight it is stronger than I am.<Close>

<Rico>
Then I'll get the doctor.<New>I'll make him come this time.<Close>

Anne
No. Stay with me, Rico.<New>Just until I fall asleep.<Close>

Anne
My stubborn boy. You have done everything I asked.<Close>
Before dawn, Anne's breathing grows quiet.<New>Rico keeps holding her hand long after it has gone cold.<Close>
When morning comes, a local Ethos priest prepares Anne for burial. Rico remains beside the empty bed in silent vigil.<New>He does not move until the rain stops.<Close>

<Rico>
Mom... I did everything you asked.<New>The flower has water. The room is warm.<New>Why wasn't it enough?<Close>
Daylight enters through the window.<New>Across the room, the watered stonebell turns its pale blue bells toward the light.<Close>

Days later, thin daylight lies across the burial ground beyond Nortune's outer wall.<New>Among its weathered markers, fresh earth and a plain wooden post bear Anne Banderas's name.<New>Only Rico and the Ethos priest stand at her grave.<Close>

ETHOS PRIEST
Anne Banderas never had much, but she shared whatever she could.<New>When a neighbor fell ill one winter, Anne brought her firewood and stayed until the fever broke.<New>Through her own long sickness, she endured with quiet courage.<New>She leaves behind her young son, Rico, and her husband, who is still fighting far from home in the war.<New>Her suffering is over now, and her soul has returned to God.<New>May she rest in His peace.<Close>
The priest lowers his head and gives Rico a final, silent blessing.<Close>

<Rico>
Mercy...<Close>
